opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kathryn Bishop (employee ID E023) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E023.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kathryn Bishop (E023) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires the role to own the system (Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist), so write is the maximum. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E023 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note listed full-time, but security records disagree). Contractors with basic training max out at read; write requires advanced training. Payroll is not owned by Engineer, so no admin. Recommend granting read, not the requested write.
reason: Kathryn Bishop (E023), an Engineer, requested write access to Payroll. Per the HR record (the authority on employment type), she is a full-time employee. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires the role to own the system, and Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Engineer, so write is the maximum. The requested level (write) is at or below that maximum, so I grant write.
